criterion.definition: On the 60 development images, the detections with score >= 0.5 of the Linux runtime are identical to those of the Windows V9 runtime in count and order per image, and no box coordinate or score differs by more than 1e-6. Raw output tensors are NOT required to be byte-identical.
criterion.supersedes: The original W62 deployment-gate text (tensors compared byte for byte). That stricter test was not met and was not waived silently: the owner accepted this criterion instead.

acceptance.basis: This measurement: V9 61/61 and retail 52/52 detections identical, maximum box/score delta 3.6e-7 (Intel) and 8.9e-7 (AMD EPYC).
acceptance.claims: Parity of the detector output only. It is not a qualification, does not change faceSafety (unknown) and does not replace the real-video measurement of the W70 journey.

pins.note: The receipt is valid only for exactly these bytes. A different value in any field refuses the platform again (fail-closed).

bridgeNote: The measurement executed the pixel-oracle bridge (measuredOracleBridgeSha256), which compiles and feeds V9 exactly as the worker bridge does (BGR, direct INTER_LINEAR resize to 448x448, NCHW float32, CPU, 2 threads, 1 stream, LATENCY, f32). The registry pins the worker bridge (workerBridgeSha256), the file that runs in production. The worker bridge was NOT executed on Linux in this measurement. Supplementary check, Windows only, one run: worker bridge versus oracle bridge on the same 60 images gave V9 raw tensors byte-identical in 60/60.

results.reading: Numerical noise of the CPU kernels (last bit of float32), not a different decision: the same faces with the same boxes, within 1e-6. Whether another CPU family keeps the same property is not measured.

evidence.runner: run-oracle-parity.mjs (repository OpenvinoPixelOracle, unmodified, batches of 30, no pairs)
